title: Malaysia Bourse Tipped To Open Under Pressure
text:
Malaysia Bourse Tipped To Open Under Pressure RTTNews Nov. 12, 2018, 06:29 PM
(RTTNews) - The Malaysia stock market has moved lower in two straight sessions, sliding more than 25 points or 1.6 percent along the way. The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index now rests just above the 1,695-point plateau and it's looking at another soft start again on Tuesday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets is soft, with weakness expected among the technology stocks and oil companies. The European and U.S. markets were down and the Asian bourse are expected to follow suit.
The KLCI finished modestly lower on Monday following losses from the financial shares, plantation stocks and industrial issues.
For the day, the index lost 11.95 points or 0.70 percent to finish at the daily low of 1,696.14 after peaking at 1,706.34. Volume was 1.633 billion shares worth 1.321 billion ringgit. There were 452 decliners and 294 gainers.
Among the actives, IHH Healthcare plummeted 3.71 percent, while MISC surged 2.64 percent, Sime Darby plunged 2.04 percent, Axiata Group tumbled 1.68 percent, IOI Corporation skidded 1.54 percent, CIMB Group dropped 1.08 percent, Tenaga Nasional retreated 1.07 percent, Maybank declined 0.97 percent, Genting shed 0.88 percent, Digi.com lost 0.67 percent, Dialog Group fell 0.60 percent, Genting Malaysia advanced 0.56 percent, Telekom Malaysia added 0.42 percent, Petronas Chemicals dipped 0.21 percent, Public Bank eased 0.08 percent and Kuala Lumpur Kepong and Petronas Gas were unchanged.
The lead from Wall Street is broadly negative as stocks moved sharply lower on Monday, extending losses from the previous session.
The Dow plunged 602.12 points or 2.32 percent to 25,387.18, while the NASDAQ dropped 206.03 points or 2.78 percent to 7,200.87 and the S&P fell 54.79 points or 1.97 percent to 2,726.22.
A sharp decline by shares of Apple (AAPL) and General Electric (GE) weighed on the markets, while concerns about the outlook for global economic growth and a continued increase in interest rates also contributed to the sell-off.
Light trading activity may have exaggerated the downward move, however, as government offices, the bond markets, and most banks were closed in observance of Veterans Day.
Crude oil shook off early gains on Monday to end lower for the 11th straight session on oversupply concerns. Crude oil futures for December, which rose to $61.28 earlier in the session, settled lower by $0.26 or 0.4 percent at $59.93 a barrel, the lowest settlement since February.
